LESSON: WHOLE NUMBERS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade one
Subject: MATHEMATICS ACTIVITIES
Strand: Numbers
Topic 1.2: Whole Numbers
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 25

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Whole Numbers, part of Numbers in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade one MATHEMATICS ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: How do we count from 1 to 20?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. Collect in purposive groups/pairs concrete objects from the immediate environment to use in counting activities. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body or appropriate assistive technology to perform given tasks. Safety precaution should be observed for all learners.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. Collect in purposive groups/pairs concrete objects from the immediate environment to use in counting activities. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body or appropriate assistive technology to perform given tasks. Safety precaution should be observed for all learners.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Whole Numbers together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Digital literacy: learner uses digital devices to play games involving numbers 1 to 50.

● Creativity: learner creates patterns with numbers up to 20.

Values:
● Respect: learner appreciates peers as they take turn in counting numbers forward up to 50.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Social cohesion: learner takes turn in counting numbers forward up to 50.

● Environmental safety: learner observes safety when collecting concrete objects from the immediate environment.

Link to other learning areas:

● The learner is able to relate the skills used in concept of reading and writing numbers in words and in symbols to functional

reading and writing in English Language Activities.

● The learner is able to relate the skills used in creating number patterns to the concept of patterns in Creative Activities.
